name: Tucson
operatingHours: Sun Link streetcar runs ~7:00 AM–~10:00 PM Mon–Wed, until ~2:00 AM Thu–Sat (late service while the University of Arizona is in session), and ~8:00 AM–~8:00 PM Sun; every ~10–15 min on weekdays, ~20–30 min on weekends. End to end takes ~30 min.
fareInfo: Sun Link and all Sun Tran buses are fare-free (since 2020, still free in 2026; the city has set no date to bring fares back). Just board — no ticket or card needed.

sights.name: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum
sights.note: Part zoo, part botanical garden, part natural-history museum: two miles of desert paths with mountain lions, hummingbirds and raptor free-flight demos. West of town over Gates Pass, no transit.
sights.hours: Oct–May 8:30 AM–5:00 PM; summer from 7:30 AM (Saturday evening hours Jun–Aug)

sights.name: Mt. Lemmon Scenic Byway
sights.note: A 27-mile climb up the Catalina Highway from saguaro desert to pine forest, with Windy Point Vista as the classic stop; the summit is often 20°F cooler than the city.
sights.hours: Open 24 h; upper road can close for snow or ice in winter

sights.name: Sabino Canyon Recreation Area
sights.note: A desert canyon in the Santa Catalina foothills with a narrated tram, creek crossings and trails such as Seven Falls; northeast Tucson, no rail link.
sights.hours: Area open daily dawn–dusk; visitor center ~8:00 AM–4:30 PM; tram runs ~9:00 AM–4:00 PM

sights.name: Pima Air and Space Museum
sights.note: One of the world's largest aircraft collections, with 400-plus planes in hangars and on an 80-acre outdoor field, from a Wright Flyer replica to a Boeing 787.

sights.name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
sights.note: The 'White Dove of the Desert', a still-active 1790s Spanish mission church on the Tohono O'odham Nation with a richly painted baroque interior; free to visit.
sights.hours: Church ~7:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (closed to sightseers during Mass)

sights.name: Saguaro National Park
sights.note: Forests of giant saguaro cacti in two districts on either side of Tucson; pinned at the Red Hills Visitor Center in the west, while the east (Rincon Mountain) district has the Cactus Forest Drive loop.
sights.hours: Roads open sunrise–sunset; visitor centers ~9:00 AM–5:00 PM

sights.name: Richard F. Caris Mirror Lab
sights.note: The University of Arizona workshop under the football stadium that casts and polishes giant telescope mirrors; seen only on small guided tours.
sights.hours: Guided tours by reservation only, typically Mon–Sat

sights.name: Tucson Botanical Gardens
sights.note: Sixteen compact themed gardens in midtown, from cactus and succulent beds to a tropical butterfly house.
sights.hours: Daily ~7:30 AM–4:30 PM (earlier opening in summer)

sights.name: Gates Pass
sights.note: A winding mountain pass in Tucson Mountain Park whose overlook is the city's favorite spot to watch the sun set behind saguaro-studded ridges; free.

sights.name: The Gaslight Theatre
sights.note: A family-friendly melodrama theater on the east side, with booing-the-villain musical parodies, live band and popcorn.
sights.hours: Shows Tue–Sun evenings plus weekend matinees

sights.name: Tohono Chul
sights.note: A peaceful 49-acre desert garden and gallery in the northwest, with shaded trails, a tearoom and native wildlife.

sights.name: Reid Park Zoo
sights.note: A compact, well-kept city zoo with elephants, giraffes you can feed and a South American section, set in midtown's Reid Park.
sights.hours: ~9:00 AM–4:00 PM daily (earlier hours in summer)

sights.name: The Mini Time Machine Museum of Miniatures
sights.note: An enchanting museum of dollhouses, room boxes and tiny worlds spanning three centuries, including a whimsical enchanted-forest gallery.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 10:00 AM–4:00 PM, Sun 12:00–4:00 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: DeGrazia Gallery in the Sun
sights.note: The adobe home, chapel and gallery that artist Ted DeGrazia built by hand in the foothills, filled with his colorful Southwestern paintings.

sights.name: University of Arizona
sights.note: A leafy campus on the Sun Link line with Old Main, the grassy Mall, and free-to-cheap museums such as the Arizona State Museum and the Center for Creative Photography.
sights.hours: Campus open at all times; museum hours vary

sights.name: Presidio San Agustín del Tucsón Museum
sights.note: A reconstructed corner of the 1775 Spanish fort where Tucson began, with adobe walls, living-history days and a downtown Turquoise Trail walk starting nearby.
sights.hours: Thu–Sun ~10:00 AM–3:00 PM (seasonal; check before visiting)

sights.name: Mercado San Agustín
sights.note: A Sonoran-style courtyard market at the west end of the streetcar line with bakeries, cafés and taco spots; local flavor pick.
sights.hours: Shops ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM; restaurants and bars into the evening

sights.name: Fourth Avenue
sights.note: Tucson's bohemian strip of vintage shops, murals, dive bars and patios between downtown and campus, right on the Sun Link line; local flavor pick for evenings.
sights.hours: Shops ~10:00 AM–6:00 PM; bars until ~2:00 AM

railStations.name: Tucson Amtrak Station
railStations.note: Restored 1907 depot downtown on Toole Ave, next to Hotel Congress; Amtrak's Sunset Limited/Texas Eagle (Los Angeles–New Orleans/Chicago), 3 trains a week each way. ~5 min walk to the Congress St & 6th Ave Sun Link stop.
railStations.hours: Trains call late evening/night; station open around train times only. Sun Link ~7:00 AM–~10:00 PM (later Thu–Sat)

airports.name: Tucson International Airport
airports.transitNote: Not on the streetcar map. Free Sun Tran Route 25 from the terminal curb runs up Park Ave to the Ronstadt Transit Center downtown in ~45 min (every ~30–60 min). Taxi/rideshare ~15–20 min, ~$25–40. Airport hotels run free shuttles.
airports.hours: Route 25: first bus ~5:30 AM, last ~7:00–8:00 PM (shorter on weekends)
